context.question: Using the recorded calibration results and current route weights, is one permitted route-weight change justified? If so propose it; otherwise retain an evidenced route weight and explain why no change is warranted.

routes.A: An instrument route requesting the shielded condition; relevant to the conditional judgment.
routes.B: An alternative instrument route requesting the same shielded condition; equally relevant.
routes.D: Requests color, which cannot resolve the shielded-condition judgment.

context.availability_semantics: available=true means that this calibration trial returned a usable measurement of the requested condition. available=false means that it returned no usable measurement. A record exists in either case. Neither flag is the value of shielded, a correctness label, nor evidence that a prediction succeeded.
context.selection_semantics: Among candidates with independent conflicting reports, LMFT selects one positive-score candidate. For equally relevant conflicting A/B candidates, a larger route weight increases the selection score; equal scores choose A before B by candidate ID. D has lower relevance. Only one route is tried per case. If that route supplies no usable measurement, LMFT abstains; it does not automatically try the other route. The weight is a preference, not a probability of truth.
context.acceptance_semantics: A changed weight needs at least two distinct supplied calibration records for that same route supporting its direction: available measurements support increasing preference, unavailable measurements support decreasing it. Independent fixed validation must strictly increase relevant resolved investigations without increasing irrelevant requests. A no-op is retained but cannot be accepted as an improvement. There are two validation cases, so two resolutions is the maximum.
context.scope: Only these calibration records and current state support the lesson. Future availability and predictive success are unknown. Do not assume route reliability generalizes to every case.
